title: Placental Matrisome Proteomic Analysis by LC-MS/MS
author: Amanpreet K. Bains
materials: Probe samples using the following primary antibodies: Anti-actin (kindly gifted by Dr. Richard O. Hynes; use at 1:5000 dilution) Anti-integrin beta-1 (kindly gifted by Dr. Richard O. Hynes; use at 1:1000 dilution) Anti-collagen III (Abcam #ab7778; use at 2 µg/mL) Anti-GAPDH (Sigma #MAB374; use at 2 µg/mL) Anti-histone H4 (Sigma #05-858; use at 1:30000 dilution) Anti-transglutaminase 2/TGM2 (Abcam #ab421; use at 2.5 µg /mL)
Detect primary antibodies using HRP-conjugated secondary antibodies: Goat anti-rabbit HRP (Invitrogen #31460; use at 8 µg /mL) Goat anti-mouse HRP (Invitrogen #31430; use at 1.6 µg/mL)
Reduce disulfide bonds using 10 mM DTT.

steps.title: Prepare Tissue Samples
steps.instruction: Weigh 45–120 mg of placenta tissue for each sample.

steps.title: Homogenize Tissue
steps.instruction: Homogenize the tissue using an OMNI Bead Ruptor at 8 m/s.

substeps.instruction: Transfer tissue into bead homogenization tubes containing four 2.8 mm ceramic beads (OMNI International #19628) and four 2.4 mm metal beads (OMNI International #19-610).
Perform three 10-second homogenization cycles with 60-second pauses between cycles.

steps.title: Enrich Extracellular Matrix Proteins
steps.instruction: Perform sequential extraction of intracellular proteins to enrich extracellular matrix (ECM) proteins using the Subcellular Protein Fractionation Kit for Tissues (Thermo Scientific #87790) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

substeps.instruction: Sequentially remove intracellular proteins in order of decreasing solubility.
Assess enrichment efficiency and intracellular protein depletion by western blot analysis.

steps.title: Solubilize and Alkylate Proteins
steps.instruction: Prepare the ECM-enriched protein pellets for digestion.

substeps.instruction: Solubilize pellets in 8 M urea prepared in 100 mM ammonium bicarbonate.
Alkylate reduced cysteines using 25 mM iodoacetamide for 30 minutes at room temperature in the dark.
Dilute samples to a final urea concentration of 2 M.

steps.title: Deglycosylate and Digest Proteins
steps.instruction: Perform enzymatic digestion of the proteins.

substeps.instruction: Deglycosylate proteins using PNGase F for 2 hours at 37°C under mild agitation.
Digest proteins with Lys-C for 2 hours at 37°C under mild agitation.
Add trypsin and incubate samples overnight at 37°C under mild agitation.
Add a fresh aliquot of trypsin the following day and incubate for an additional 2 hours at 37°C.

steps.title: Desalt and Quantify Peptides
steps.instruction: Clean and quantify the resulting peptides.

substeps.instruction: Desalt peptides using Pierce Peptide Desalting Spin Columns according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Reconstitute peptides in 95% HPLC-grade water, 5% acetonitrile, and 0.1% formic acid.
Quantify peptide concentration using the Pierce Quantitative Colorimetric Peptide Assay Kit (#23275).

steps.title: Configure LC-MS/MS Instrumentation
steps.instruction: Set up the LC-MS/MS system using a Q Exactive HF mass spectrometer and UltiMate 3000 RSLC nanosystem with a Nanospray Flex Ion Source.

substeps.instruction: Load samples onto a Waters nanoEase M/Z C18 trap column (100 Å, 5 µm, 180 µm × 20 mm).
Separate peptides using a Waters BEH C18 analytical column (130 Å, 1.7 µm, 75 µm × 150 mm).
Prepare mobile phases: Solvent A (0.1% formic acid in water) and Solvent B (0.1% formic acid in 80% acetonitrile).

steps.title: Perform LC-MS/MS Analysis
steps.instruction: Inject 1 µg peptide per sample and run chromatography at a flow rate of 300 nL/min.

substeps.instruction: Run LC gradient: 5% B (0–3 min), 8% B (at 6 min), 8–40% B (6–85 min), 40–95% B (85–90 min), hold at 95% B until 94.8 min, and re-equilibrate at 5% B until 105 min.

steps.title: Acquire Mass Spectrometry Data
steps.instruction: Configure the mass spectrometer for data acquisition.

substeps.instruction: Acquire full MS survey scans over a mass range of 350–1400 m/z at a resolution of 120,000 with an AGC target of 3.0 × 10^6 and a maximum injection time of 50 ms.
Select the 20 most intense precursor ions (charge states 2–5) for fragmentation.
Fragment precursor ions using higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) with a normalized collision energy of 28%.
Acquire tandem MS/MS spectra at a resolution of 30,000 with an AGC target of 1.0 × 10^5, an ion selection threshold of 2.0 × 10^4 counts, and a maximum injection time of 120 ms.
Apply dynamic exclusion for 30 seconds using a 1.2 m/z exclusion window.
